subject: dwarfRifleman
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: dwarf rifleman with braided beard and blunderbuss.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm checking the identity cues: the braided orange beard, helmet with goggles, and blunderbuss all read clearly, but the gun's grip and pointing direction in the front view look awkward and need adjusting.

The bigger issue is the signpost overlapping the arm in the front view, hiding the "IRONFORGE" text. I'm working out whether repositioning the signpost (shifting its x/z coordinates) or rotating the sign to point the other direction would clear the overlap with the hand.

Let me settle on a modest position: shift the post to around x=0.58, z=-0.5, with the sign pointing in the +x direction and a tighter outline, keeping the crate nearby at a reasonable distance so it doesn't look floating off the base.

Updating post to z=-0.5, sign at -0.47, plane at -0.4585. Looking over the top view now, checking hand poses and fingerless gloves look fine. Checking face coverage from beard fur cards, eyes still visible, head proportions reasonable for a dwarf, nose fine. Checking back view too — tabard, gun stock bar, and left hand placement all seem acceptable.

The tan torus ring floating at the chest looks like a loose rope coil but is passable, and the shoulder pauldron gold pip positions seem a bit off but tolerable. In the front view, the right arm and gun grip look fine despite the forearm being obscured by the bell.

The biggest composition issue is scale: the base (1.37 x 1.72) and the white rock chunks dominate the frame more than the character does. I'm considering shrinking the base from 1.3 to around 1.15 and scaling down the rocks, though that risks disrupting prop placement.

I'll shrink the rock scale from roughly 0.05-0.10 down to about 0.04 each, cutting their size by about 70%, and tweak the ring radius slightly.

Looking at the legs now, the knee guards are rendered as silver spheres that look like floating ball bearings rather than armor plates, especially awkward in the three-quarter view. I'm thinking of flattening them into gold-rimmed shield plates with adjusted scale and ring size, and reconsidering their z-offset so they sit properly against the shin instead of floating ahead of the leg.

I'll pull the guard offset in from 0.085 to 0.07 and reduce depth from 0.04 to 0.03 so they seat closer to the leg surface. The hips, helmet brim, brow tufts, and hand pose all look fine as-is; the orange sideburn tuft near the ear is a minor oddity I'll leave alone, and the harmless dead scatter(0) call in the beard code can stay. The brass crest strip running over the helmet top reads correctly as a decorative feature.

I'm checking the gun's grip and orientation in the three-quarter view — the stock hangs back past the elbow, which is acceptable, though I consider raising the muzzle for a more shouldered look before deciding to skip it. I'll avoid rescaling the whole head for proportion reasons since that cascades into too many position changes, and instead focus my edits on moving the signpost, seating the knee guard better, shrinking the base rocks, and tightening the base scale, plus repositioning the beard-clasp gem that currently sits awkwardly in front of the beard ring.

I'm nudging the gem to sit seated on the ring surface, adjusting its depth and size slightly, and fixing a similar small offset on the back tabard relative to the hips box depth. I also check whether the gun or base needs resizing for better framing, but since the gun's bell tip nearly overhangs the base edge, I decide to shrink only the rocks rather than the whole base, then start writing out the precise edits for the rock scaling values.

I'm now rewriting the knee guard geometry to be flatter — adjusting the blob's position and scale, lowering the floating torus ring's height, and adding a gold stud at its center. Then I move on to editing the signpost block, identifying the exact rod and extrusion lines that need replacing for the wooden post structure.

For the signpost itself, I'm adjusting the extruded arrow shape, the sign's texture plane and its tilt orientation, plus the snow blob and iron torus accent, and considering shifting the post's x-position slightly to see how it reads.

Settling on post at x=0.55, z=-0.5, with the sign plane centered around x=0.595, z=-0.4585 and width 0.27 — slight overhang beyond the base edge is acceptable since the post itself stays grounded.
